newsitem.title: USA: SmithKline says antiviral agent study favorable.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline says antiviral agent study favorable.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc said Monday a multinational, dose-finding study showed that the antiviral agent famciclovir is effective in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B with a safety profile comparable to a placebo.
This is the first report of successful treatment of chronic hepatitis B with a new-generation nucleoside analogue in a large placebo-controlled clinical study, the drug maker said.

Famciclovir treatment resulted in a rapid, dose-dependent suppression of hepatitis B virus replication, lead study researcher Professor Christian Trepo, who is based in Lyon, France, said in a statement released here.
"In all famciclovir treatment groups, the effect on hepatitis B virus DNA levels was evident within one week of therapy ... and was maintained throughout the 16-week treatment period," he said.
"The normalization of liver enzymes was sustained eight months after the 16-week treatment period in 50 percent of patients in the famciclovir 500 mg group," he said.

"This is the first time that a prolonged benefit has been shown after short-term therapy with a nucleoside analogue. It may indicate that famciclovir has, in effect, 'incapacitated' the hepatitis B virus multiplication," he added.
